item.title: SQL Techniques for Isolating Numeric Data From Alphanumeric Strings
item.description:
“SQL Techniques for Isolating Numeric Data From Alphanumeric Strings”

How can one effectively purge non-digit characters from character strings within a SQL database, presenting only the sequential numeric components? Several advanced techniques exist for this common data cleaning task, ranging from procedural User-Defined Functions (UDFs) to set-based Recursive Common Table Expressions (RCTEs) and specific functions available in different SQL dialects like MySQL or Oracle.

Here we examine multiple accepted solutions providing robust ways to isolate numerical sequences.

item.title: SQL String Aggregation: Efficiently Concatenate Column Values
item.description:
“SQL String Aggregation: Efficiently Concatenate Column Values”

When working with relational databases, a common task involves consolidating string values from multiple rows into a single, delimited string. This is particularly useful for reporting or creating summary views. For instance, you might want to list all product names associated with a specific category, separated by commas. This post delves into various SQL techniques to achieve this, focusing on robustness and clarity.

item.title: SQL Server String Splitting Techniques: Functions and Methods
item.description:
“SQL Server String Splitting Techniques: Functions and Methods”

SQL Server String Splitting Functions and Methods

The core challenge is to transform a single string containing multiple values, separated by a specific character or string, into a table format where each value resides in its own row. This facilitates easier querying, aggregation, and manipulation of the data.

Here are several methods discussed, each with its own advantages and considerations:

Solution 1: Recursive CTE for String Splitting

This method utilizes a Common Table Expression (CTE) with recursion to iteratively find and extract substrings based on a delimiter. It’s a clean approach for SQL Server 2005 and later.

item.title: Oracle SQL String Aggregation: LISTAGG, XMLAGG, and More
item.description:
“Oracle SQL String Aggregation: LISTAGG, XMLAGG, and More”

This question delves into various techniques for concatenating strings from multiple rows into a single string, a common requirement in database operations. We will examine several Oracle SQL functions and clauses, providing practical examples for each.

String Aggregation Methods in Oracle SQL

Several methods exist for aggregating strings in Oracle SQL, each with its own advantages and use cases.

1. LISTAGG Function

The LISTAGG function, available from Oracle 11g Release 2, is a modern and often preferred method for string aggregation. It allows for ordered concatenation of strings.
